text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will hold a meeting today in Cairo to discuss how to move the Middle East peace process forward. U.S. envoy Dennis Ross is carrying proposals that Israel refrain from building new settlements. Mubarak is also due to meet Portugal's president.

- Mubarak on Tuesday will receive an invitation from Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati to attend the Islamic conference in Tehran in December. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said that he will meet Velayati today and they will discuss the agenda of the summit.
- Egyptian economic delegation in Paris headed by Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid will discuss 25 projects for $15 billion investment.

- Egyptian cabinet says Egypt stresses its commitment to a just and comprehensive peace in the Middle East; it reviews the trip to Singapore, Malaysia and China made by Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri and sets up a committee to follow through to increase investments and exports and implement the agreements made during the trip.

- Minister of Finance Mohieddin el-Gharib tells the parliament that there are steps to lower government spending and that there will be no new taxes in the new fiscal year. He said the aim is to rationalise spending without affecting social services. He said the budget for 1997/98 was 83.3 billion pounds, up 7.5 percent from the previous year.
